2026-11-11 source-pin maintenance: registryContentHash refreshed after content fixes to six pinned source questions, approved by the project owner (coding-trust step 9). 2026-11-11 source-pin maintenance: registryContentHash refreshed after the JavaScript test hardening of coding-trust step 10, approved by the project owner. Five pinned source questions gain checks for behavior their text and rubric criteria already describe, and the new checks join the rubric groups that state that behavior. Deep equal: three checks (different kinds of object, the same set of keys, NaN, -0 and RegExp details); the reference solution now compares Object.prototype.toString tags, so a Date no longer equals {}, as its edge cases already said. Debounce: one check for the last call's this and all of its arguments; the summary loses its page copy. LRU cache: two checks (an update makes a key the most recent; an update at capacity evicts nothing); the returns text says that size() is a method and in which order keys() lists the keys. Concurrency map: the limit check is renamed 'rejects a limit below 1' and accepts a rejection as well as a synchronous throw, which the async starter could not meet; two checks cover refilling a slot as soon as it frees up and starting no new items after a fail-fast error, and the concurrency-bound and error-strategies groups each gain one criterion for them. Once: one check for a wrapped function that returns undefined. Question hashes are re-pinned for all five; the debounce prompt loses only the page copy, the other prompts are unchanged; time limits and revisions are unchanged. Pin maintenance under registry version 1.1.0, not a new release.

This is not a new release approval.

criteria: The parent selects or clears every child in one transition.

No children selected means the parent is unchecked.

Repeated transitions must not duplicate selected IDs.

criteria: Trim the draft and reject an empty or whitespace-only comment.
Append a valid root node with a stable unique ID and an empty children array.
Clear the root draft only after a successful insertion.
Preserve every existing node and its relative order.
groups.title: Root comment boundary

criteria: Clicking Reply opens exactly one editor beneath that comment.
Opening another editor transfers ownership instead of duplicating drafts.
Cancel closes the editor and clears its draft.
Submitting a non-empty reply inserts it under the owning parent and closes the editor.
groups.title: Single reply owner

criteria: Locate parents by stable ID at any depth rather than by a hard-coded level.
Rebuild only the ancestor path to the changed node.
Preserve every unaffected branch by value and order.
Generate globally unique IDs for nested and root nodes.
groups.title: Arbitrary-depth update

criteria: Expose the comment list as a tree and every comment as a treeitem with its one-based aria-level.
Give each Reply control an accessible name that identifies its comment.
Give the reply input a stable label associated with the owning comment.
After Post or Cancel, return focus to the Reply control that opened the editor.
Announce successful insertion in a polite status region without moving reading position.
groups.title: Accessible tree and focus

checks.name: Round 1 · Valid root insertion preserves the tree
Round 2 · Reply is inserted under its owner
Round 3 · Replying to a reply creates a third level
Round 4 · Recursive structure and insertion are announced

criteria: Move only selected source items to the target list.
Preserve the relative order of moved and existing items.
Clear moved selections after a successful transfer.
Disable transfer actions when their source has no selection.
groups.title: Atomic transfer

criteria: Move-left is the inverse of move-right for the selected IDs.
An item can exist in exactly one list at a time.
No-op actions do not reorder lists or change selection.
Use stable item IDs rather than display labels or array indexes.
groups.title: Bidirectional consistency

criteria: Transfer every selected item exactly once in source order.
A second action during the same state cannot duplicate items.
Selections belong to their source list and never cross list ownership.
Render an accurate item count for each list after every transition.
groups.title: Bulk boundaries

criteria: Give both lists distinct accessible names and group each row with its checkbox label.
Give transfer controls directional accessible names independent of arrow glyphs.
Preserve native checkbox keyboard behavior.
Announce the number and direction of moved items in a polite status region.
groups.title: Accessible transfer workflow

checks.name: Round 1 · Selected item moves once
Round 2 · Item can return without duplication
Round 3 · Two selected identities move in source order
Round 4 · Direction and result are announced
